chain_words.nuance: to reduce the quality or enjoyment of something, without total loss
to harm something so that it works less well
to damage something so badly that it is no longer usable
to destroy violently over a wide area
to cause complete destruction, often with emotional impact

explanation: These words all express the core idea of ruining something, but they differ in degree, from a mild loss of quality to complete devastation.

usage_notes.difference: 'Damage' describes harm that may be partial or repairable; 'wreck' implies that the object is so badly harmed that it is no longer usable.
